verses.zh: 耶稣又用比喻对他们说：
verses.en: Jesus spoke[NOTE:1] to them again in parables, saying:
notes: Grk “And answering again, Jesus spoke.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation.

verses.zh: 「天国好比一个王为他儿子摆设娶亲的筵席，
verses.en: “The kingdom of heaven can be compared to a king who gave a wedding banquet for his son.

verses.zh: 就打发仆人去，请那些被召的人来赴席，他们却不肯来。
verses.en: He sent his slaves[NOTE:1] to summon those who had been invited to the banquet, but they would not come.
notes: See the note on the word “slave” in 8:9.

verses.zh: 王又打发别的仆人，说：『你们告诉那被召的人，我的筵席已经预备好了，牛和肥畜已经宰了，各样都齐备，请你们来赴席。』
verses.en: Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “Look! The feast I have prepared for you is ready.[NOTE:1] My oxen and fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.”’
notes: Grk “Behold, I have prepared my meal.” In some contexts, however, to translate ἄριστον (ariston) as “meal” or “dinner” somewhat misses the point. L&N 23.22 here suggests, “See now, the feast I have prepared (for you is ready).”

verses.zh: 那些人不理就走了；一个到自己田里去；一个做买卖去；
verses.en: But they were indifferent and went away, one to his farm, another to his business.

verses.zh: 其余的拿住仆人，凌辱他们，把他们杀了。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] rest seized his slaves, insolently mistreated them, and killed them.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 王就大怒，发兵除灭那些凶手，烧毁他们的城。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] king was furious! He sent his soldiers, and they put those murderers to death[NOTE:2] and set their city[NOTE:3] on fire.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Grk “he sent his soldiers, destroyed those murderers.” The verb ἀπώλεσεν (apōlesen) is causative, indicating that the king was the one behind the execution of the murderers. In English the causative idea is not expressed naturally here; either a purpose clause (“he sent his soldiers to put those murderers to death”) or a relative clause (“he sent his soldier who put those murderers to death”) is preferred.
The Greek text reads here πόλις (polis), which could be translated “town” or “city.” The prophetic reference is to the city of Jerusalem, so “city” is more appropriate here.

verses.zh: 于是对仆人说：『喜筵已经齐备，只是所召的人不配。
verses.en: Then he said to his slaves, ‘The wedding is ready, but the ones who had been invited were not worthy.

verses.zh: 所以你们要往岔路口上去，凡遇见的，都召来赴席。』
verses.en: So go into the main streets and invite everyone you find to the wedding banquet.’

verses.zh: 那些仆人就出去，到大路上，凡遇见的，不论善恶都召聚了来，筵席上就坐满了客。
verses.en: And those slaves went out into the streets and gathered all they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

verses.zh: 王进来观看宾客，见那里有一个没有穿礼服的，
verses.en: But when the king came in to see the wedding guests, he saw a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.

verses.zh: 就对他说：『朋友，你到这里来怎么不穿礼服呢？』那人无言可答。
verses.en: And he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But he had nothing to say.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “he was silent.”

verses.zh: 于是王对使唤的人说：『捆起他的手脚来，把他丢在外边的黑暗里；在那里必要哀哭切齿了。』
verses.en: Then the king said to his attendants, ‘Tie him up hand and foot and throw him into the outer darkness,[NOTE:1] where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth!’
notes: The Greek term translated “darkness” (σκότος) is associated with Tartarus in Aeschylus, Eumenides 72; other references to the darkness of death and the underworld can be found throughout the classical literature as far back as Homer. BDAG 932 s.v. σκότος 1 states: “Of the darkness of the place of punishment far removed fr. the heavenly kingdom (Philo, Exsecr. 152 βαθὺ σκότος. Cp. Wsd 17:20; PsSol 14:9.—σκ. κ. βόρβορος ‘gloom and muck’ await those who are untrue to the Eleusinian Mysteries, Ael. Aristid. 22, 10 K.=19 p. 421 D. Of the darkness of death and the underworld in Hom. and the Trag. As the domain of evil spirits PGM 36, 138; Theoph. Ant. 2, 7 [p. 110, 5]) τὸ σκ. τὸ ἐξώτερον the darkness outside Mt 8:12; 22:13; 25:30.”

verses.zh: 因为被召的人多，选上的人少。」
verses.en: For many are called, but few are chosen.”

verses.zh: 当时，法利赛人出去商议，怎样就着耶稣的话陷害他，
verses.en: Then the Pharisees[NOTE:1] went out and planned together to entrap him with his own words.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.
Grk “trap him in word.”

verses.zh: 就打发他们的门徒同希律党的人去见耶稣，说：「夫子，我们知道你是诚实人，并且诚诚实实传　神的道，甚么人你都不徇情面，因为你不看人的外貌。
verses.en: They sent to him their disciples along with the Herodians,[NOTE:1] saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.[NOTE:2] You do not court anyone’s favor because you show no partiality.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Herodians are mentioned in the NT only once in Matt (22:16 = Mark 12:13) and twice in Mark (3:6; 12:13; some mss also read “Herodians” instead of “Herod” in Mark 8:15). It is generally assumed that as a group the Herodians were Jewish supporters of the Herodian dynasty (or of Herod Antipas in particular). In every instance they are linked with the Pharisees. This probably reflects agreement regarding political objectives (nationalism as opposed to submission to the yoke of Roman oppression) rather than philosophy or religious beliefs.

Teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Very few comments are as deceitful as this one; they did not really believe this at all. The question of the Pharisees and Herodians was specifically designed to trap Jesus.
Grk “And it is not a concern to you about anyone because you do not see the face of men.”

verses.zh: 请告诉我们，你的意见如何？纳税给凯撒可以不可以？」
verses.en: Tell us then, what do you think? Is it right[NOTE:1] to pay taxes[NOTE:2] to Caesar[NOTE:3] or not?”
notes: Or “lawful,” that is, in accordance with God’s divine law. On the syntax of ἔξεστιν (exestin) with an infinitive and accusative, see BDF §409.3.

According to L&N 57.180 the term κῆνσος (kēnsos) was borrowed from Latin and referred to a poll tax, a tax paid by each adult male to the Roman government.sn This question concerning taxes was specifically designed to trap Jesus. If he answered yes, then his opponents could publicly discredit him as a sympathizer with Rome. If he answered no, then they could go to the Roman governor and accuse Jesus of rebellion.
Or “to the emperor” (“Caesar” is a title for the Roman emperor).

verses.zh: 耶稣看出他们的恶意，就说：「假冒为善的人哪，为甚么试探我？
verses.en: But Jesus realized their evil intentions and said, “Hypocrites! Why are you testing me?

verses.zh: 拿一个上税的钱给我看！」他们就拿一个银钱来给他。
verses.en: Show me the coin used for the tax.” So[NOTE:1] they brought him a denarius.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate their response to Jesus’ request for a coin.

Here the specific name of the coin was retained in the translation because not all coins in circulation in Palestine at the time carried the image of Caesar. In other places δηνάριον (dēnarion) has been translated simply as “silver coin” with an explanatory note.sn A denarius was a silver coin worth approximately one day’s wage for a laborer. The fact that they had such a coin showed that they already operated in the economic world of Rome. The denarius would have had a picture of Tiberius Caesar stamped on it.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「这像和这号是谁的？」
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said to them, “Whose image[NOTE:2] is this, and whose inscription?”
notes: Grk “And he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

Or “whose likeness.”sn In this passage Jesus points to the image (Grk εἰκών, eikōn) of Caesar on the coin. This same Greek word is used in Gen 1:26 (LXX) to state that humanity is made in the “image” of God. Jesus is making a subtle yet powerful contrast: Caesar’s image is on the denarius, so he can lay claim to money through taxation, but God’s image is on humanity, so he can lay claim to each individual life.

verses.zh: 他们说：「是凯撒的。」耶稣说：「这样，凯撒的物当归给凯撒；　神的物当归给　神。」
verses.en: They replied,[NOTE:1] “Caesar’s.” He said to them,[NOTE:2] “Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “they said to him.”
Grk “then he said to them.” τότε (tote) has not been translated to avoid redundancy.
Jesus’ answer to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s was a both/and, not the questioners’ either/or. So he slipped out of their trap.

verses.zh: 他们听见就希奇，离开他走了。
verses.en: Now when they heard this they were stunned,[NOTE:1] and they left him and went away.
notes: Grk “they were amazed.”

verses.zh: 撒都该人常说没有复活的事。那天，他们来问耶稣说：
verses.en: The same day Sadducees[NOTE:1] (who say there is no resurrection)[NOTE:2] came to him and asked him,[NOTE:3]
notes: See the note on Sadducees in 3:7.
This remark is best regarded as a parenthetical note by the author.
Grk “and asked him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 「夫子，摩西说：『人若死了，没有孩子，他兄弟当娶他的妻，为哥哥生子立后。』
verses.en: “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies without having children, his brother must marry the widow and father children[NOTE:1] for his brother.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “and raise up seed,” an idiom for fathering children (L&N 23.59).

A quotation from Deut 25:5. This practice is called levirate marriage (see also Ruth 4:1-12; Mishnah, m. Yevamot; Josephus, Ant. 4.8.23 [4.254-256]). The levirate law is described in Deut 25:5-10. The brother of a man who died without a son had an obligation to marry his brother’s widow. This served several purposes: It provided for the widow in a society where a widow with no children to care for her would be reduced to begging, and it preserved the name of the deceased, who would be regarded as the legal father of the first son produced from that marriage.

verses.zh: 从前，在我们这里有弟兄七人，第一个娶了妻，死了，没有孩子，撇下妻子给兄弟。
verses.en: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died, and since he had no children he left his wife to his brother.

verses.zh: 第二、第三、直到第七个，都是如此。
verses.en: The second did the same, and the third, down to the seventh.

verses.zh: 末后，妇人也死了。
verses.en: Last[NOTE:1] of all, the woman died.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 这样，当复活的时候，她是七个人中哪一个的妻子呢？因为他们都娶过她。」
verses.en: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had married her.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “For all had her.”

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「你们错了；因为不明白圣经，也不晓得　神的大能。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] answered them, “You are deceived[NOTE:2] because you don’t know the scriptures or the power of God.
notes: Grk “And answering, Jesus said to them.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation.
Or “mistaken” (cf. BDAG 822 s.v. πλανάω 2.c.γ).

verses.zh: 当复活的时候，人也不娶也不嫁，乃像天上的使者一样。
verses.en: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels[NOTE:1] in heaven.
notes: Most witnesses have “of God” after “angels,” although some mss read ἄγγελοι θεοῦ (angeloi theou; א L ƒ13 28 33 892 1241 1424) while others have ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ (angeloi tou theou; W Γ Δ 0102 0161 565 579 M). Whether with or without the article, the reading “of God” appears to be a motivated addition. A few significant witnesses lack the adjunct (B D Θ 0233 ƒ1 700 sa); this coupled with strong internal evidence argues for the authenticity of the shorter reading.sn Angels do not die, nor do they eat according to Jewish tradition (1 En. 15:6; 51:4; Wis 5:5; 2 Bar. 51:10; 1QH 3.21-23).

verses.zh: 论到死人复活，　神在经上向你们所说的，你们没有念过吗？
verses.en: Now as for the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “spoken to you by God, saying.” The participle λέγοντος (legontos) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他说：『我是亚伯拉罕的　神，以撒的　神，雅各的　神。』　神不是死人的　神，乃是活人的　神。」
verses.en: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?[NOTE:1] He is not the God of the dead but of the living!”[NOTE:2]
notes: A quotation from Exod 3:6.

He is not God of the dead but of the living. Jesus’ point was that if God could identify himself as God of the three old patriarchs, then they must still be alive when God spoke to Moses; and so they must be raised.

verses.zh: 众人听见这话，就希奇他的教训。
verses.en: When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.

verses.zh: 法利赛人听见耶稣堵住了撒都该人的口，他们就聚集。
verses.en: Now when the Pharisees[NOTE:1] heard that he had silenced the Sadducees,[NOTE:2] they assembled together.[NOTE:3]
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.
See the note on Sadducees in 3:7.
Grk “for the same.” That is, for the same purpose that the Sadducees had of testing Jesus.

verses.zh: 内中有一个人是律法师，要试探耶稣，就问他说：
verses.en: And one of them, an expert in religious law,[NOTE:1] asked him a question to test[NOTE:2] him:
notes: Traditionally, “a lawyer.” This was an expert in the interpretation of the Mosaic law.
Grk “testing.” The participle, however, is telic in force.

verses.zh: 「夫子，律法上的诫命，哪一条是最大的呢？」
verses.en: “Teacher, which commandment in the law is the greatest?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or possibly “What sort of commandment in the law is great?”

verses.zh: 耶稣对他说：「你要尽心、尽性、尽意爱主―你的　神。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said to him, “‘Love[NOTE:2] the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “You will love.” The future indicative is used here with imperatival force (see ExSyn 452 and 569).
A quotation from Deut 6:5. The threefold reference to different parts of the person says, in effect, that one should love God with all one’s being.

verses.zh: 这是诫命中的第一，且是最大的。
verses.en: This is the first and greatest[NOTE:1] commandment.
notes: Grk “the great and first.”

verses.zh: 其次也相仿，就是要爱人如己。
verses.en: The second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Lev 19:18.

verses.zh: 这两条诫命是律法和先知一切道理的总纲。」
verses.en: All the law and the prophets depend[NOTE:1] on these two commandments.”
notes: Grk “hang.” The verb κρεμάννυμι (kremannumi) is used here with a figurative meaning (cf. BDAG 566 s.v. 2.b).

verses.zh: 法利赛人聚集的时候，耶稣问他们说：
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] the Pharisees[NOTE:2] were assembled, Jesus asked them a question:[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.
Grk “asked them a question, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is somewhat redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 「论到基督，你们的意见如何？他是谁的子孙呢？」他们回答说：「是大卫的子孙。」
verses.en: “What do you think about the Christ?[NOTE:1] Whose son is he?” They said, “The son of David.”[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on Christ in 1:16.tn Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

It was a common belief in Judaism that Messiah would be the son of David in that he would come from the lineage of David. On this point the Pharisees agreed and were correct. But their understanding was nonetheless incomplete, for Messiah is also David’s Lord. With this statement Jesus was affirming that, as the Messiah, he is both God and man.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「这样，大卫被圣灵感动，怎么还称他为主，说：
verses.en: He said to them, “How then does David by the Spirit call him ‘Lord,’ saying,

verses.zh: 主对我主说：你坐在我的右边，等我把你仇敌放在你的脚下。
verses.en: “‘The Lord said to my lord,[NOTE:1] “Sit at my right hand,until I put your enemies under your feet”’?[NOTE:2]
notes: The Lord said to my lord. With David being the speaker, this indicates his respect for his descendant (referred to as my lord). Jesus was arguing, as the ancient exposition assumed, that the passage is about the Lord’s anointed. The passage looks at an enthronement of this figure and a declaration of honor for him as he takes his place at the side of God. In Jerusalem, the king’s palace was located to the right of the temple to indicate this kind of relationship. Jesus was pressing the language here to get his opponents to reflect on how great Messiah is.
A quotation from Ps 110:1.

verses.zh: 大卫既称他为主，他怎么又是大卫的子孙呢？」
verses.en: If David then calls him ‘Lord,’ how can he be his son?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “how is he his son?”

verses.zh: 他们没有一个人能回答一言。从那日以后，也没有人敢再问他甚么。
verses.en: No one[NOTE:1] was able to answer him a word, and from that day on no one dared to question him any longer.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
